title: nudgeSize == 0 disables the payout but not the inflow or the flush: value migrates into an un-metered container the owner cannot stop filling
description: setNudgeSize(0) is documented at two NatSpec sites (:40-41, :269-270) as 'disables the feature'. It disables the PAYOUT (_snapshotRewards:801 gates its own balance read on `qualifies`; _payRewards:831 skips zero amounts) but NOT the inflow (permissionless collectNudge keeps funding the streamer buffer; production NudgeRatchet donates on schedule) and NOT the flush (the loop at :528-536 sits immediately above _snapshotRewards doing the opposite - it does not read `qualifies`). Value therefore migrates OUT of the streamer and INTO the batchMinter during the nominally-disabled period, in the wrong container, invisibly.
impact: A 'disabled' nudge accumulates ~30,000 units over a 30-day disable at 1,000/day inflow, delivered as ONE un-metered lump to whoever wins the first re-enabled qualifying batch. *** WORDING CORRECTED 2026-07-30 (remediation pass): 'THERE IS NO RETURN PATH' WAS IMPRECISE. Read: THERE IS NO WAY TO STOP THE INFLOW, AND NO METER ON THE DESTINATION. *** NudgeStreamer is the container with no exit - no withdrawal, no pause, no deregistration. The DESTINATION, BatchNFTMinterMultiToken, DOES have rescueERC20 (:386-389, onlyOwner, no token restriction, callable while paused). So the flush moves value OUT OF A NO-RESCUE CONTAINER AND INTO A RESCUABLE ONE, and the operator HAS a remedy for the accumulated lump once it has landed. What the owner has no lever for is the ACCUMULATION ITSELF: collectNudge is permissionless, the production donor is on a schedule, and the flush does not read `qualifies`. That is the finding, and it still supports Low. (This further WEAKENS the 'no return path' framing rather than strengthening it - recorded because the distinction changes the operator's options.)
law3: NON-OBVIOUS FOOTGUN => in scope. Two NatSpec sites say 'disables the feature'; _snapshotRewards gates its own balance read on `qualifies`; the flush sits immediately above doing the opposite. A competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised.
honestLimit: NO VALUE IS LOST. Nudge pots are funded by externally-derived yield on protocol-owned capital (OWNER CORRECTION 2026-07-26), so mis-sizing is misallocation/opportunity cost, NEVER economic loss. Funds stay in protocol-controlled contracts throughout. Also, the flush is not the CAUSE of the lump - a quiet period > `duration` makes _accrued hit its `buffer` cap anyway. The flush's distinct contribution is that accumulation happens DURING the disabled period, in the wrong container, invisibly.
severityNote: Low. Classified on the CUSTODY-LOCATION and OPERATOR-EXPECTATION footgun alone. Carries NO value-leak limb, and the KI #16 pot-size limb is STRUCK per the sanitizer's narrowing.
recommendation: Gate the flush loop at :528-536 on `qualifies` - the SAME change is PART 1 of L-01's fix, and it closes THIS finding in full - and correct the two NatSpec sites (:40-41, :269-270) to state precisely what setNudgeSize(0) does and does not stop. NOTE: the gate alone does NOT complete L-01, which additionally needs the per-token try/catch (L-01 part 2) to remove the brick for QUALIFYING batches.

crossReferences.why: SAME code site, DIFFERENT consequence. Do NOT collapse - upstream decision 2. A reader who only saw the availability framing would never learn the accumulation happens.
